30 Day Chart Challenge 2026 Day 19: Evolution
Baby names over time

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggthemes)
library(ggtext)
```

```{r}
# Download directly
url <- "https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/state/namesbystate.zip"
download.file(url, "namesbystate.zip")
unzip("namesbystate.zip", exdir = "namesbystate")

# Check what files are in there
list.files("namesbystate") %>% head(10)
or_names <- read_csv("namesbystate/OR.TXT",
                     col_names = c("state", "sex", "year", "name", "n"))
```

```{r}
or_names <- or_names %>% 
  group_by(year, sex) %>% mutate(prop = n/ sum(n))
```

```{r}
or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 10) %>%
  summarise(top10_share = sum(prop))


or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 10) %>%
  summarise(top10_share = sum(prop)) %>% 
  tail(10)

or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(total_oregon = sum(n)) %>%
  tail(5)

or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(year/10)*10) %>%
  group_by(decade, name) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(total, n = 1, by = decade)

or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "M") %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(year/10)*10) %>%
  group_by(decade, name) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(total, n = 1, by = decade)
```


```{r}
# Step 1: Get decade top names
decade_names <- or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(year/10)*10) %>%
  group_by(decade, name) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(total, n = 1, by = decade)

# Step 2: Get unique name list
name_list <- unique(decade_names$name)

# Step 3: Get full year-by-year history for those names
highlight_data <- or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F", name %in% name_list)

# Step 4: Get peak year and n for each name for labels
name_peaks <- highlight_data %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Check
name_peaks

# Keep decade info with each name
decade_tops <- or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F") %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(year/10)*10) %>%
  group_by(decade, name) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(total, n = 1, by = decade)

# Get just the unique names for filtering
top_name_list <- decade_tops %>% pull(name) %>% unique()

# Full year-by-year history for those names
highlight_data <- or_names %>%
  filter(sex == "F",
         name %in% top_name_list) %>%
  mutate(is_olivia = name == "Olivia")

# Check
decade_tops  # shows which name topped each decade
highlight_data %>% count(name)  # shows data available for each name



```

```{r}
windowsFonts(georgia = windowsFont("Georgia"))
p <- ggplot() +
  # Grey spaghetti lines
  geom_line(data = highlight_data %>% filter(!is_olivia),
            aes(x = year, y = n, group = name),
            color = "darkgrey", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Olivia highlighted
  geom_line(data = highlight_data %>% filter(is_olivia),
            aes(x = year, y = n),
            color = "#846092", linewidth = 1.5) +
  # Labels at peak for grey lines
  geom_text(data = name_peaks %>% filter(name != "Olivia"),
            aes(x = year, y = n, label = name),
            size = 4, family = "georgia", color = "#222222",
            vjust = -0.8) +
  # Olivia label at peak
  geom_text(data = name_peaks %>% filter(name == "Olivia"),
            aes(x = year, y = n, label = "Olivia"),
            size = 5, family = "georgia", color = "#846092",
            fontface = "bold", vjust = -0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1910, 2024, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Oregon's Most Popular Baby Girl Names, From Mary to <b style='color:#6a3d8f'>Olivia</b>",
    subtitle = "Annual count at each name's peak, 1910–2024",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = "Data: SSA Baby Names by State | #30DayChartChallenge Day 19\nCreated by: Lyndsay Miles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0ecf5", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0ecf5", color = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey88", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.title = element_markdown(family = "georgia", size = 20,
                              face = "bold", color = "#1a1a1a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "georgia", size = 14,
                                 color = "grey40"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "georgia", size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(family = "georgia", size = 10,
                                hjust = 1, color = "grey50"),
    plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 20, 20)
  )

ggsave("img/cc_2026_day19.png", p,
       width = 10, height = 6, 
       dpi = 300)
```
#Day19 of the #30DayChartChallenge | Evolution (Timeseries)
Today I looked at the evolution of popular baby girl names in Oregon since 1910. Olivia is the new favorite, but what's going on with Linda in the 1940s?
